questions.q: What is the formula used to calculate the area of a circle?
questions.a: The formula is A = π × r². A student who says "A = 2 × π × r" is confusing the area formula with the circumference formula, which measures the distance around the edge, not the space inside.

questions.q: If you have two circles, one with a radius of 2 cm and one with a radius of 4 cm, is the area of the larger circle double the area of the smaller one? Explain why or why not.
questions.a: No, it is not double; it is four times larger. A student who says "yes" does not understand that the radius is squared (r²), so doubling the radius (2 × 2) results in a 4-fold increase in area (2² = 4).

questions.q: Calculate the area of a circular garden with a radius of 7 meters (use π = 22/7).
questions.a: Step 1: Identify radius (r = 7). Step 2: Square the radius (7 × 7 = 49). Step 3: Multiply by 22/7 (49 × 22/7 = 7 × 22 = 154). Answer: 154 m². If a student gets 44, they likely calculated 2 × π × r (circumference) instead of the area.

questions.q: If you are given the area of a circle, can you find the radius? How would you start?
questions.a: Yes, by dividing the area by pi and then finding the square root of the result. A student who tries to divide the area by 2 or by pi alone does not understand the inverse relationship of squaring a number.

questions.q: Is it better to use π = 3.14 or π = 22/7 when the radius is a multiple of 7? Why?
questions.a: It is better to use 22/7 because it allows for easy cancellation of the denominator when the radius is 7 or 14, making the calculation simpler and more accurate. A student who insists on 3.14 may struggle with long multiplication decimals unnecessarily.

questions.q: Create a real-world scenario where knowing the area of a circle is more important than knowing its circumference.
questions.a: A good answer would involve buying paint for a circular tabletop or choosing the size of a circular rug to cover a floor. An answer involving fences or rope refers to circumference, showing the student still confuses boundary length with internal space.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The area of a circle is the total amount of flat space ______ within its curved boundary.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are helping your friend cut a ______ piece of card paper for a school project.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to calculate the area of a circle given its radius and identify that area is measured in square units.
